newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds rally as U.S inflation fears recede.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds rally as U.S inflation fears recede.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed stronger in heavy trading on Wednesday as investors reacted with glee to economic data showing minimal inflationary pressures in the U.S. economy, traders said.
The U.S. Labor Department reported that the monthly Consumer Price Index (CPI) rose 0.1 percent in June compared with a 0.1 percent increase in May.
The so-called core rate, excluding volatile food and energy costs, also rose just 0.1 percent, the slowest pace for the first half of the year in 32 years.
Analysts said markets were quick to jump on the results.
"The market is basically buoyed by every single piece of evidence this week that has shown either neutral or bond-friendly results," said Andrew Pyle, economist with ABN-AMRO Hoare Govett.
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond rose C$1.43 to C$119.91 to yield a record low of 6.483 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond climbed 30/32 to yield 6.47 percent. The spread between the bonds narrowed to one basis point from a spread of two basis points at the close on Tuesday.
Pyle said the strong gains wiped away technical weakness hanging over the market earlier this week.
But a weaker Canadian dollar offset some of the gains in the bond market. The dollar closed at C$1.3739 (US$0.7278) on Wednesday after opening at C$1.3727 (US$0.7285).
Analysts said U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's Humphrey-Hawkins testimony on July 22 would be the next large hurdle for the Canadian bond market.
"The next test is the Humphrey-Hawkins testimony, but until then I think we can expect bonds to push a little higher," said Harvinder Kalirai, Canadian analyst with New York-based I.D.E.A.
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond jumped C$0.78 to C$109.88 to yield 5.910 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond rose 16/32 to yield 6.19 percent.
The negative spread between the two benchmark bonds widened to 28 basis points from a spread of 24 basis points at the close on Tuesday.
The three-month cash T-bill yielded 3.23 percent against its U.S. equivalent, which yielded 5.19 percent.
